threads.thread_goal: Align on MVP scope, success metrics, and responsibilities.

messages.text: Kicking off the unified self-service support portal work. We have 30 days to get an MVP live that actually reduces inbound calls and works well on web and mobile. I will start a draft of the MVP scope and metrics in Self-Service Portal MVP Scope and Metrics so we can track T1 there and keep scope tight. For now, I am thinking: home page with clear entry points, searchable FAQ, basic how-to articles, and a simple contact handoff to existing channels. Please react here with anything you see as absolutely essential for day one so we can capture it in A1 without overloading the first release.

From the calls I handle, the biggest wins for launch would be: password reset and login issues, billing and payment questions, and basic account changes like address updates. If those flows are easy to find from the home page and covered in the FAQ, we should see fewer calls quickly. I will map these into the Top Call Drivers and FAQ Mapping sheet so they are reflected in A1 as must-haves, and we can keep more niche topics for later.

For content, I suggest we keep MVP scope to: FAQ entries for the top call drivers, a small set of how-to guides for the most common tasks, and a short announcements area for known issues. Anything like long-form troubleshooting or edge-case policies can go into a post-launch backlog. I will align T6 and T7 with whatever we lock into A1 so non-technical staff can maintain it easily.

On the experience side, I will keep the MVP navigation very lean: a home page with clear tiles for the main topics, a global search, and a visible link to contact options. I will document this in Portal Information Architecture and User Flows and sync it with A1 so we do not add extra sections for now. We can still leave room in the IA for future modules without building them yet.

From a build perspective, if we keep MVP to home, FAQ, search, and a simple contact handoff, I can cover T5 and T9 with a basic responsive layout and straightforward search. Anything like user forums, chatbots, or deep account management flows should be explicitly marked as out of scope in A1 so we do not accidentally start wiring them in.

For success metrics, I propose we focus on a small set that we can realistically measure in the first weeks. My suggestion: percentage of calls deflected for the top call drivers, portal usage for unique visitors and sessions, and task completion rate for key flows like password reset. I will add these into A1 under T1 and work with 472507 on how they map into the analytics setup later.

I have added a first pass of the MVP feature list into A1 based on this thread: 1) Home page with tiles for top topics and search, 2) FAQ listing and detail pages for the top call drivers, 3) A small set of how-to guides, 4) Simple contact handoff to existing channels, 5) Basic analytics events for page views and search usage. I have also listed non-MVP ideas like chatbots, user forums, and advanced account changes in a parked section. Before we call this final, can each of you confirm that this covers your must-haves for day one and that you are ok with the parked list staying out of MVP?

I checked the MVP list in A1. As long as password reset, login issues, billing, and address changes are clearly visible from the home page and searchable, I am comfortable. Things like rare technical errors or unusual billing disputes can wait. I am fine with chatbots and forums being parked for now, as long as we keep a backlog note so we can revisit after we see how customers use the portal.

From a content angle, the MVP list in A1 works for me. I will focus T7 on FAQs and how-tos for the topics 6370 highlighted. Longer troubleshooting trees and marketing-heavy content can stay in the parked section. That will also make T6 simpler, since the workflow for a smaller set of article types is easier to roll out to non-technical editors.

I am aligned with the MVP scope in A1. The IA in A4 will mirror that: no extra sections for community, advanced account tools, or marketing campaigns in this first release. I will leave placeholders in the sitemap for future modules but keep them inactive so they do not create expectations for launch.

Confirmed from my side as well. The current MVP list in A1 is feasible within the 30-day window if we avoid adding extra interactive components. I will scope T5 and T9 strictly around those pages and basic search. Anything beyond that I will log as follow-up items so we do not blur the line between MVP and later phases.

I have added the three primary metrics into A1 under T1: 1) Call deflection rate for the top call drivers, 2) Portal usage measured as unique visitors and sessions, 3) Task completion rate for key flows like password reset and billing questions. For now, I suggest we treat NPS or satisfaction surveys as nice-to-have for later, so they are listed in the parked section. If no one objects, we can treat these three as our main launch metrics.

Thanks all. Based on confirmations here, I am marking the MVP feature list in A1 as agreed and the extra items as explicitly parked for post-launch. We will treat the three metrics 59590 outlined as our primary success measures for T1 and feed them into the analytics work later. If anything critical comes up, we can still raise it in the twice-weekly scope check-ins, but the default is to keep this list stable.

All good from support. I will keep feeding real call patterns into A2 so we can refine FAQs without changing the agreed MVP scope. That should help us hit the call deflection metric without needing new features before launch.

I will align the content backlog for T7 with the final MVP list in A1 and share a short summary of which articles map to which metric, so we can see how each piece of content supports call deflection and task completion.

I will update A4 to clearly label which parts of the IA are in MVP and which are future, so there is no confusion when we review designs. That should also help keep design feedback focused on what we are actually shipping in the next 30 days.

I will break down T5 and T9 into smaller dev tasks aligned with the agreed MVP pages and share an outline later today. That way we can track progress against the scope in A1 and avoid surprises near the deadline.
I will also start a simple view in the analytics dashboard artifact to show the three agreed metrics, so when T10 is implemented we already know how we want to read the data post-launch.

threads.thread_goal: Prioritise top call drivers and confirm initial FAQ set.

messages.text: I have pulled the last 60 days of support logs and drafted the Top Call Drivers and FAQ Mapping in A2 for T2. The top 20 reasons cover login and password, billing and payments, address and contact changes, order status, and a few technical issues. I have grouped them into proposed FAQ topics and added a first pass at question wording. Please review and comment so we can decide which topics make the MVP FAQ set.

Thanks for the sheet. I see a clear pattern around a few clusters: access issues, billing, account details, and order tracking. For T7, I suggest we treat those four clusters as mandatory FAQ sections for MVP. The lower-volume topics like rare technical errors and unusual billing disputes can be grouped into a single general troubleshooting article or left for later. I will add a column in A2 to flag my recommendation per topic.

Looking at A2 with the metrics in mind, I agree with focusing on the clusters that drive the most volume and frustration. For the first release, I would prioritise FAQs that directly support the call deflection metric: anything that currently leads to repeat calls or long handle times. I will add a simple impact score in A2 so we can see which topics are likely to move the needle most.

From an IA perspective, it will be easier for users if we keep the number of top-level FAQ categories small. If we go with access, billing, account details, and orders as the main buckets, I can reflect that in A4 and the navigation. More niche topics can live under those or in a general help section later.

For implementation, it would help if we keep the initial FAQ set to a manageable number of articles so T5 and T9 do not get overloaded. Maybe we can agree on around 25 FAQs and 10 how-tos as in T7, mapped to the top clusters in A2. Anything beyond that can be drafted but not necessarily published for MVP.

From the system side, there is no hard limit on the number of FAQs, but more content means more to maintain and more to track in analytics. I support the idea of focusing on the top clusters in A2 for MVP and treating the rest as backlog. That will also make it easier to configure T10 and A7 around a smaller set of key topics.

I have added a support pain score in A2 based on how often customers call back or escalate. Access, billing, account details, and orders clearly stand out. I agree those should be the main FAQ sections. For the rare technical issues, I am ok with a single general article that sets expectations and points people to contact us if needed.

Based on the scores in A2, here is a concrete proposal for the MVP FAQ set for T7: 1) Access and login: 8 FAQs plus 3 how-tos, 2) Billing and payments: 7 FAQs plus 3 how-tos, 3) Account details: 5 FAQs plus 2 how-tos, 4) Orders and deliveries: 5 FAQs plus 2 how-tos. That gives us 25 FAQs and 10 how-tos, matching T7. The remaining topics go into a backlog tab in A2. If everyone is ok with this, we can treat these four clusters as the initial MVP FAQ topics.

This breakdown works well with the metrics we defined. These four clusters map directly to the main call drivers and will be easy to track in A7. I support treating them as the initial MVP FAQ set and leaving the rest in the backlog tab for later iterations.
I will reflect these four clusters as the main FAQ categories in A4 and the navigation. That should keep the experience consistent with what users see in the portal and what we track in A7.
From dev side, this set is manageable. I will make sure the FAQ templates in T5 and the search filters in T9 support these four categories out of the box, so we do not need extra work later.

On content ownership, I suggest we keep it simple: 561463 owns the structure and quality of all FAQ and how-to content, while 6370 is the primary reviewer for accuracy and clarity from the support side. For more specialised topics like billing policies, we can note a secondary owner from the business teams in A2, but they will not be editing directly in the portal. If you both agree, we can record that as the ownership model for MVP.

I am comfortable owning the content structure and editing, with 6370 as the main reviewer. I will update A2 and A8 to reflect that: content owner as 561463, accuracy reviewer as 6370, and subject-matter contacts listed where needed. That should also make T6 and T7 clearer.
Works for me. I will plan time each week to review new or updated articles and log any recurring issues I see from calls back into A2 so we can keep the FAQs aligned with what customers actually ask.
With ownership clarified, I will make sure the training materials in T11 explain this model clearly so the wider support team knows who to contact for content changes and how to suggest new FAQs.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in information architecture, UX approach, and visual style.

messages.text: I have uploaded the first version of the IA and wireframes into Portal Information Architecture and User Flows for T3. The structure mirrors the four main FAQ clusters plus a home page and search results. I have also started a basic style guide draft aligned with our existing brand and the Content Style, Tone, and Accessibility Guide. Please review the flows for search, FAQ browsing, and contact handoff so we can confirm the navigation and UX approach.

I walked through the FAQ and article pages in A4. The layout works well for the content templates I have in mind for T6 and T7. One suggestion: can we make the article metadata and last-updated date more visible, so users trust that the information is current? That also helps reinforce the governance model in A8.

From a support perspective, the flows in A4 look straightforward. I like that search is prominent and that the main categories match what we see in A2. One request: on the contact handoff, can we show a short note about expected response times so customers do not call again immediately after submitting a form?

From the dev side, the IA in A4 is implementable with our current stack. The navigation is simple enough that T5 and T9 can reuse standard components. For accessibility, I will need clear guidance on heading structure, focus states, and contrast from A3 so we can bake that into the templates early.

I have checked the flows in A4 against the technical plan in A5. The navigation and page types align with what we can support in the first release. For mobile, we should confirm that the key interactions like search, filters, and contact handoff are fully usable on smaller screens, since we are reusing existing auth and CRM components.

Good points. I will update the article template in A4 to surface last-updated date and owner more clearly, and I will align the typography and spacing with A3 so it remains readable. For the contact handoff, I will add a short text block where we can show expected response times, and I will make sure it is easy to update via content rather than code.

Perfect. If the response time note is editable content, I can manage it through the templates in T6. I will also make sure the tone and reading level follow A3 so the portal feels consistent with our other channels.
Thanks for adding the response time note. That should reduce repeat calls. I will help draft the wording so it matches what we tell customers on the phone.

On accessibility, I have added notes in A4 and the style guide draft for heading hierarchy, minimum contrast ratios, focus outlines, and tap targets. These follow the rules in A3. For mobile, I am designing the layouts mobile-first so that search, filters, and contact options are easy to reach with one hand.

That helps a lot. I will implement the templates in T5 and T9 following those guidelines and run basic checks with screen readers and keyboard navigation. If we find anything that needs deeper review, we can flag it for the compliance team.

Given the updates, I am comfortable saying the proposed navigation structure and key user flows in A4 are aligned with the technical plan and constraints. Unless there are strong objections, we can treat this IA as the baseline for MVP and avoid structural changes later.
I am ok with locking the IA in A4 for MVP. The content templates and workflows in T6 and T7 will follow this structure.
No objections from support. The flows in A4 match how customers usually think about their issues, so I am happy to go ahead with this structure for MVP.

Great, I will mark the IA in A4 as final for MVP and focus T8 on refining the visual style and interaction details within this structure. I will also keep the accessibility and mobile requirements from A3 front and centre in the prototypes.

To summarise the requirements: we are committing to a responsive, mobile-friendly experience where all key flows work on small screens, and we are applying the accessibility rules from A3 from the start. We will still ask the compliance team to review a prototype, but for MVP we will treat these as non-negotiable requirements.

Understood. I will treat the mobile and accessibility requirements as part of the definition of done for T5 and T9 and log any issues we find during implementation so we can address them before the pre-launch review.

threads.thread_goal: Confirm technical architecture, integrations, and analytics setup.

messages.text: I have drafted the technical architecture and integration approach in Technical Architecture and Integration Plan for T4. The portal will be a lightweight web layer that reuses our existing authentication and CRM systems, with no new core platforms. I have also outlined a first pass at analytics events and how they will feed into the Portal Analytics and Call Deflection Dashboard for T10. Please review and call out any concerns before we lock this in.

I have gone through A5. The proposed architecture is workable from the implementation side. For T5 and T9, I will build the front-end as a separate layer that calls existing auth and CRM endpoints. One thing we should clarify is error handling when those systems are slow or unavailable, so the portal fails gracefully instead of confusing users.

From a content perspective, the architecture in A5 looks fine as long as the CMS integration allows us to manage FAQ and how-to content without needing code changes. For analytics, I would like to track which articles are most viewed and which searches return no results, so we can improve content over time.

Looking at A7 and the metrics we agreed in A1, I suggest we standardise a small set of events for T10: page views by template type, search queries and results, clicks on contact options, and completion of key tasks like password reset. That will give us enough data to estimate call deflection without overcomplicating the setup.

On the support side, the main thing I care about is that we can see whether customers are actually solving their issues or still calling us. If A7 can show trends for the top call drivers and highlight where people search but do not click or quickly go to contact, that will help us adjust FAQs and scripts.

Good call on error handling. I will update A5 to include patterns for timeouts and fallback messages when auth or CRM are slow. For MVP, we can show a clear message and a link to contact options rather than leaving users stuck. Longer term, we might explore retries or queueing, but that is beyond this 30-day window.
If A5 documents those patterns, I can implement them in T5 and T9. I will also log any recurring integration issues so we can share them with IT operations and adjust before launch.

For CMS integration, the plan in A5 is to use our existing WebCMS so that 561463 can manage FAQ and how-to content directly. I will confirm with IT operations that this approach is acceptable and that we are not introducing new platforms. For analytics, I will add the events 59590 suggested into A7 and T10 so we have a clear list to implement.

That works for me. As long as the WebCMS setup supports the templates from T6 and T7, I can handle content updates without needing dev time. For analytics, article views and search terms will be especially useful for our content review cadence in A8.

I have updated A7 with a simple reporting view that highlights the three main metrics plus search behaviour and contact clicks. For reporting cadence, I suggest a weekly review for the first month after launch, then we can move to bi-weekly once things stabilise.
Weekly reviews sound good. I can bring call centre observations to those sessions so we can compare what we see in A7 with what we hear on the phones.

Given the feedback, I propose we approve the architecture in A5 as the baseline for MVP: portal front-end layer, reuse of existing auth and CRM, WebCMS for content, and the documented error handling patterns. Any larger changes would go into a later phase. If there are no objections, we can treat this as agreed and move ahead with T4, T5, T9, and T10 based on this design.
No objections from dev. I will proceed with T5 and T9 following the architecture in A5 and keep you posted on any integration risks.
I am aligned as well. The architecture in A5 supports the content workflows we need for T6 and T7.

On analytics, can we confirm that the events we listed in A7 for T10 are the ones we will implement for MVP and that we will review them weekly post-launch? That will help set expectations with the stakeholders who care about the metrics.

Yes, let us formalise that. For MVP, we will implement the events in A7 for page views, search queries and results, contact clicks, and key task completions as part of T10. We will run a weekly metrics review for at least the first month after launch, then adjust the cadence if needed.
Great, I will update A7 to reflect the agreed events and cadence so stakeholders have a single reference.

threads.thread_goal: Plan pre-launch checks, training, and go-live date.

messages.text: I have drafted the pre-launch checklist and timeline in Pre-Launch Content and UX Review Checklist for T12, and updated Knowledge Base Governance and Workflow for T6. The checklist covers content accuracy, broken links, formatting, UX walkthroughs, and basic accessibility checks. I have also mapped these to the MVP scope in A1 so we can confirm what must be ready for go-live. Please review so we can agree on readiness criteria and training needs.

I have added UX walkthrough steps into A6 for the main flows in A4: search, FAQ browsing, article reading, and contact handoff. For each, we will check both desktop and mobile, plus basic accessibility behaviours. This should give us a clear view of whether the experience matches what we agreed in the IA and style guide.

For the pre-launch review in T12, I can run through the portal using real call scenarios and log anything confusing in A6. That will help us catch gaps where customers might still call us even though the portal exists.

I have started drafting the training deck and quick-reference guide for T11. They explain the MVP scope from A1, the main FAQ topics from A2, and how the support team should use the portal during calls. Once we finalise the checklist in A6, I will add a section on what is considered ready for go-live so expectations are clear.

From dev side, I will use A6 as the reference for what needs to be fixed before launch. For T5 and T9, I can commit to resolving critical issues like broken navigation, search errors, and major layout problems. Minor visual tweaks might need to wait for a follow-up release if they risk the date.

Looking at A6 and A1 together, I suggest we define go-live readiness as: 1) All MVP pages and flows from A1 implemented and passing the checklist in A6, 2) No critical integration or security issues from A5, 3) Initial analytics events from A7 and T10 firing correctly on key pages, 4) Support team trained using T11. Does that capture the essentials, or are we missing anything important?

I would add one more point: content ownership and workflow from A8 must be in place, with clear owners for each FAQ cluster and a review cadence agreed. Otherwise, content could drift quickly after launch. I can update A6 to include a check for that.

From support, I would like the readiness criteria to include a short pilot period where a few agents use the portal in parallel with normal calls before we promote it widely. That way we can catch any major issues without impacting SLAs.
I can incorporate a short pilot into the training plan in T11. We can run a few sessions with selected agents, then gather feedback and adjust content or flows before the full go-live announcement.

Agreed on the ownership point. I will update the readiness criteria in A6 to include: content owners and reviewers defined in A8, and at least one review cycle completed for the MVP articles. With that, I think the checklist now fully reflects the MVP scope in A1 and the governance we need.
I have updated A6 accordingly. For T12, we will run the full checklist one week before the planned go-live date and log any critical fixes with owners and due dates.

Given the updated checklist and the MVP scope in A1, I propose we reconfirm that we are still targeting the same MVP feature set for go-live and that we will use A6 as the single source of truth for readiness. Any items outside A1 will be treated as nice-to-have and will not block launch.
Confirmed from dev. I will treat A1 and A6 as the boundaries for what must be done before launch. Anything else will go into a follow-up backlog.
I am aligned as well. The training materials in T11 will focus on the MVP scope in A1 and the readiness criteria in A6 so the support team knows exactly what to expect at launch.

On content ownership readiness, I have confirmed in A8 that each FAQ cluster has a named content owner and reviewer, and that they are aware of the review cadence. We can consider that part of the checklist covered for launch.

I confirm I am ready to act as reviewer for the support-related content after launch, as documented in A8. I will also share feedback from the pilot and early calls so we can keep improving the articles.

With scope and readiness criteria confirmed, and content ownership in A8 ready, we are in a good position to hit the 30-day go-live. Let us use A6 as our checklist in the final week and keep this thread updated as we close out T6, T11, and T12.
